title: Avant-garde and Oliver Jackson's fire at the zoo
summary: Baron defends free playing and recalls Oliver Jackson Jr.'s description of an AACM concert.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Yeah. Do it at the end of the piece, to finish the piece. So it’s like she did that for me once on the streets of New York. I mean she’s another person, she does these amazing things and it’s totally like, what’s Art Baron doing in there, but it’s like, it’s got such a heart and soul. It’s not like let’s do something far out and we’ll call it new music. And that’s what’s great about it. And that’s why I’ve had this really great career that I’ve had to play with. You know I used to worry like if someone, like that Harlem Blues and Jazz or something like that, that we’d play something avante garde or something like that, oh what’s he doing. And it even happened once with us, we played with this guy George Gruntz who has a big band from Switzerland. We were playing some out stuff. Like this piano player I play with, [inaudible] I used to play with Oliver Jackson Jr., do you know him?

The drummer, yeah, he was a great friend. And he was cool about all kinds of things. And he worked with George Wein and the Newport All Stars, like he was the road manager. And he was just this great guy. So he was in Europe and he had played on the same stage with some group like, who was that saxophone quartet, you know, the very modern one.
Hamiet Bluiett — anyway — or maybe it was Lester Bowie or something like that.
Oh like the Chicago, the AACM.

Exactly, right. And I loved that stuff. And I said, “Ollie, man, that’s great, you play with those guys, and he only did two sections of the concert. And how’d they sound?” And he said, “Oh man it was great,” he said, “it was like a fire at the zoo.”

I loved that. I mean I always felt that music, you know, you could be fooled sometimes but I always felt people that were serious about it and were really making music, or the people that had learned the form and then wanted to be free of it, let’s say, that’s one way
of playing free music. It just sort of coming from a place where you had a disciplined amount, but it was so funny, a fire at the zoo, you know that sound.
